definitions.explanation: A flat piece of unused land covered in grass and weeds, especially one in or near a town where children play. Informal and everyday in tone.

examples.japanese: {原|はら}っぱ⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{遊|あそ}ぶ→遊ぶ：00550_asobu⟧。
examples.english: To play in the open field.
There is a wide grassy lot behind the house.

examples.japanese: {子|こ}ども⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{頃|ころ}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、⟦{近所|きんじょ}→近所：01318_kinjo⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{原|はら}っぱ⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{日|ひ}が{暮|く}れる→日が暮れる：16774_higakureru⟧⟦まで→まで：00490_made⟧⟦{野球|やきゅう}→野球：04727_yakyuu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦していた→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: When I was a child, I played baseball in the neighborhood field until the sun went down.

notes:
{原|はら} (field, plain) plus the informal suffix っぱ. The word carries a nostalgic, childhood flavor and appears often in stories about growing up.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {原|はら}っぱ⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{遊|あそ}ぶ→遊ぶ：00550_asobu⟧: to play in the field
- ⟦{草|くさ}っ{原|ぱら}→草っ原：30153_kusappara⟧: a grassy patch (a related informal word with the parts reversed)
- ⟦{広|ひろ}い→広い：00704_hiroi⟧{原|はら}っぱ: a wide open field

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{野原|のはら}→野原：14417_nohara⟧: field, meadow — more neutral and literary, often out in the countryside
- ⟦{空|あ}き{地|ち}→空き地：15270_akichi⟧: vacant lot — emphasizes that the land is unused or awaiting development, with no suggestion of grass
